critical_code_review_comments: server.py `check_aging` re-uses the same `cutoff` for two different guards (arrival-age AND last-reminder-age). This means once a reminder is sent, another one won't fire until aging_hours passes again — which happens to be the desired 24h cooldown by coincidence. Consider a dedicated `reminder_cooldown_hours` setting instead of coupling it to aging threshold.

GuardDashboard `hoursSince` uses browser Date.now() vs server `arrived_at`. Clock skew between client and backend could show a package as aging one poll before the backend agrees (aging_count still 0). Cosmetic only.

get_photo endpoint accepts `auth` as a query param, which is fine for img tags but the token ends up in server access logs. Consider signed short-lived URLs or Referer/Origin checks for hardened deployments.

upload_photo silently falls back to ext='jpg' for non-allowed extensions instead of returning 400 — an actual malicious upload with wrong extension would still be stored (content-type from client is trusted). Low risk since only guard/admin can upload.
